chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
And give its due on the day of its harvest

They all said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from the charity; he gives the poor man a handful after a handful, and from the harvest a handful after a handful until he finishes, and he gives the guard a known wage, and he leaves from the palm trees Mi'a Farat or Umm Jarour, and what is in the enclosure for the guard, the bunch, the two bunches, and the three, for guarding it.'

key_terms.أُمَّ جُعْرُور: A specific type or quantity of palm produce
key_terms.الْقَبْضَة: A handful (unit of measure for distribution)
key_terms.مِعَى فَأْرَة: A specific type or quantity of palm produce

ai.seo_question: How is the 'due' (haqq) calculated and distributed from agricultural harvest according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the practical application of agricultural zakat by prescribing incremental giving (handful by handful) until the harvest is cleared, ensuring the donor's sincerity and ease. The narration further details the customary rights of the harvest guard, including a fixed wage and the retention of specific date clusters for their protection, reflecting the socio-economic norms of early Shia jurisprudence. This hadith highlights the integration of divine obligation with practical agricultural management in Shia legal tradition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa from Hareyz, from Zurara, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Abu Baseer,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[6:141] and give the due of it on the day of its harvest

, and they all (narrators) said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘This is from the charity (Zakāt) given to the poor, the bunch after the bunch, and the handful after the handful until he is free, and he gives to the guard a known recompense, and he leaves from the palm tree Mi’a Farat or Umm Jarour (two types) and he would leave for the guard what happens to be in the wall, the bunch and the two bunches, and the three, for him having guarded it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim and abu Basir who has said the following:
“About the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious,
‘Give His right on the day of its harvest . . .,’ [6:142]

all of them have said that abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘It is of charity (Zakat) that which is given to the destitute, a bunch after bunch and from fruits handful after handful until all fruits are picked up from trees. The guard has a definite right, which is left for him of the trees. Palm trees like Mi‘afarah and ‘Umm Ja‘rur are left alone. One, two or three trees are left for the guard because of his guarding.’”
